question: Identify the dance style recognized for its spiritual devotion and connection to the Vaishnavite movement.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sattriya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form of India, originating from Assam and deeply rooted in the **Vaishnavite movement**.
 
• This dance form was introduced in the 15th century by the saint-scholar **Srimanta Sankardev**, a key figure in the Vaishnavism revival in Assam.
 
• **Sattriya** was traditionally performed in the monasteries (Satras) as a form of religious expression and devotion to Lord Krishna.
 
• It incorporates themes from **Bhagavat Purana** and other ancient scriptures, emphasizing spirituality and divine love.
 
• The dance style was officially recognized as a classical dance of India by the **Sangeet Natak Akademi** in 2000.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vaishnavite Movement:**

 
 
• The Vaishnavite movement in Assam was led by Srimanta Sankardev, promoting devotion to **Lord Vishnu or Krishna**.
 
• It emphasized **Bhakti (devotion)**, egalitarianism, and the use of art forms like music, dance, and drama for spiritual expression.
 
 
 
• **Satras:**
 
 
• Satras are **Vaishnavite monasteries** established by Srimanta Sankardev and his disciples.
 
• These monasteries serve as centers for spiritual and cultural learning, focusing on art, literature, and religious practices.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya Dance Features:**
 
 
• The dance style combines **hand gestures (mudras), foot movements, expressions, and rhythmic patterns**.
 
• It includes solo, group, and dramatic performances, often with mythological narratives.
 
 
 
• **Recognition as Classical Dance:**
 
 
• Sattriya was recognized as a **classical dance** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, highlighting its cultural and historical significance.
 
• This recognition helped bring Sattriya from the monasteries to broader platforms, both nationally and internationally.
